runs.text: Earnings are the weakest dimension: revenue is exposed to commodity prices and plant uptime, and fixed plant costs turn a modest revenue move into a large EBITDA move. In FY2024 revenue fell 22.91% and EBITDA fell 36.36%, 1.59 times as fast, because direct operating expenses fell only 8.32%; EBITDA then recovered to USD 210.85 million in FY2025 and USD 224.73 million for the last twelve months. Customers contract for less than one year at fixed prices, the top two took 28% of FY2025 sales, and a turnaround or outage hits a single site. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 113; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B2; calculation B4; calculation B13

Leverage is moderate and the debt is fixed rate, which is the strongest support. Total debt to EBITDA ranged from 1.95x in FY2023 to 3.18x in FY2024 and stood at 2.54x on the last-twelve-months basis, with net leverage of 1.83x; because the notes carry a fixed coupon, cover of EBITDA to cash interest moved only with EBITDA, from 5.24x at the low in FY2024 to 6.10x. Debt of USD 569.74 million includes finance lease obligations, and no principal falls due before June 2028. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 104–106; calculation B1; calculation B13

Cash conversion is adequate and improving but rests on rising capital spending. Free cash flow was positive in every period, USD 219.33 million in FY2023, USD 98.84 million in FY2025 and USD 148.71 million for the last twelve months, equal to 78.03%, 46.87% and 66.17% of EBITDA. Cash capital expenditures rose from USD 50.8 million in FY2025 to USD 88.08 million over the last twelve months, and the 2026 estimate sits 66.89% to 82.7% above FY2025 spending, so conversion depends on the East Dubuque expansion and reliability projects paying back. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation B5; calculation B6; calculation B13

Liquidity is adequate for the next two quarters and the refinancing window is distant but not remote. Liquidity of USD 203.4 million at September 30, 2026 is cash of USD 158.2 million plus availability under an undrawn asset-based facility; after the declared distribution of USD 18.9 million and fourth-quarter capital spending, cash would stand at USD 101.18 million to USD 110.18 million before any operating cash flow in the quarter. The notes mature 575 days after the as-of date and become a current liability in mid-2027, so refinancing capacity will be tested at the point the nitrogen cycle is least predictable. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 104; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation B7; calculation B13

Financial policy is the second weakness. Distributions of USD 281.36 million in FY2023 and USD 125.99 million in FY2025 exceeded free cash flow and were met from cash, about 39% went to CVR Energy and Icahn Enterprises, and the board can change the policy at any time. Customer prepayments lifted deferred revenue to USD 83.93 million at September 30, 2026, equal to 53.06% of the cash balance, so part of the cash buffer is owed in product and the working-capital inflow will reverse as deliveries are made. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation B10; calculation B11; calculation B13

Event risk is concentrated in control. The owners are considering strategic options that could involve the Partnership, with no terms stated, and a sale of the Icahn interest in CVR Energy could be a change of control under the notes with a repurchase offer of about USD 555.5 million; liquidity covers 36.61% of it. Supply and services from CVR Energy also depend on common control, so a change would reach operations as well as debt, and the executed debt documents that would settle the terms are not in the evidence. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 115; calculation B8; calculation B13

cells.text: Two nitrogen fertilizer plants: Coffeyville, Kansas (gasification of pet coke; ammonia 1,300 tons a day; UAN 3,100 tons a day) and East Dubuque, Illinois (natural gas; ammonia 1,075 tons a day; UAN 950 tons a day)
UAN 61.76%, ammonia 23.61%, urea products 6.17% and other revenue 8.46% of net sales of USD 606.038 million; the text gives UAN 67% and ammonia 24% including freight
Wholesale to retailers and distributors; contracts generally fixed price with terms under one year; top two customers 28% of FY2025 net sales
Pet coke at Coffeyville, about 36% of it from CVR Energy's refinery in 2025 (46% in 2024, 43% in 2023); natural gas at East Dubuque from third parties
Higher net sales in the first half (planting season) and lower in the second half
East Dubuque turnaround from late August to mid-October 2026 with an ammonia expansion expected to add about 5% capacity, to be tested in the fourth quarter
Cash flow follows nitrogen prices and uptime with annual repricing; related-party feedstock and services tie operations to CVR Energy

runs.text: Strengths, ranked. First, fixed-rate notes of USD 550.0 million with no maturity before June 2028 and an undrawn facility: interest cost is fixed, so cover of 6.10x moves only with EBITDA, and no refinancing is needed for 575 days. Second, moderate leverage of 1.83x net on last-twelve-months EBITDA, which leaves room to absorb a moderate decline. Third, positive free cash flow in every period, USD 148.71 million over the last twelve months, which funds capital spending and most distributions. Fourth, liquidity of USD 203.4 million, which comfortably exceeds the known calls of the fourth quarter. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation B1; calculation B5; calculation B13

Weaknesses, ranked. First, volatile EBITDA on high fixed costs: EBITDA fell 36.36% in FY2024 on a revenue fall of 22.91%, which is the path to a liquidity or refinancing problem. Second, owner control with a variable distribution policy that exceeded free cash flow in two of three fiscal years, so creditors rely on cash rather than retained earnings. Third, change-of-control exposure of about USD 555.5 million with owners reviewing options. Fourth, rising capital spending and a working-capital inflow from prepayments that will reverse. Fifth, unseen debt documents and no ratings or market prices. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B2; calculation B8; calculation B11; calculation B13

runs.text: No specified transaction is in the evidence. CVR Energy and Icahn Enterprises state that they are considering potential strategic transactions, which may include strategic options involving the Partnership, with no assurance that any will develop and no terms, price, financing or timetable given. fields.value: Financial foundation for Cvr Partners, Lp (CVR Partners, LP in its filings; issuer id uan-1425292), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and cover from the eight supplied filings and releases, FY2023 to FY2025 and the nine months to 2026-09-30, in USD thousands as printed and US$m in the money tables.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate and the only borrowed debt matures in 2028, but EBITDA swings with fertilizer prices and plant downtime and most cash is distributed, so creditor protection rests on the cash balance and a small asset-based facility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was USD 411.55 million at September 30, 2026, or 1.83x last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 224.73 million against 2.37x at the end of 2025, and total debt was USD 569.74 million. Quarter-end cash of USD 158.19 million was lifted by customer prepayments, and the declared distribution of USD 18.9 million would take net leverage to 1.92x once paid on November 23, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt to EBITDA was 1.95x in FY2023, 3.18x in FY2024, 2.70x in FY2025 and 2.54x for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, and net debt to EBITDA was 1.79x, 2.67x, 2.37x and 1.83x. Debt moved by only USD 22.43 million over the period, almost all of it finance lease obligations first recorded in 2024, so the swings come from EBITDA, which fell from USD 281.1 million in FY2023 to USD 178.9 million in FY2024 before recovering. The notes carry a fixed coupon, so EBITDA to cash interest of 8.25x, 5.24x, 5.74x and 6.10x moved with EBITDA alone: creditors carry commodity-cycle risk on a stable debt balance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third quarter of 2026 shows how quickly cover can fall: EBITDA was USD 19.72 million against USD 70.62 million a year earlier, with turnaround expenses of USD 26.84 million against USD 1.23 million, yet nine-month EBITDA of USD 204.56 million stayed above USD 190.68 million. The East Dubuque turnaround ended in mid-October 2026, so the lost output is behind the company, but the issuer expects the expanded capacity to be tested in the fourth quarter. The fourth quarter of 2025, derived at USD 20.17 million of EBITDA, also carried a turnaround, at Coffeyville, so two of the four quarters in the last-twelve-months figure were weak and that figure already absorbs both.

After cash capital expenditures of USD 64.51 million the free cash flow of USD 193.88 million funded distributions of USD 110.45 million and left cash USD 88.95 million higher. The working-capital inflow reverses as product ships, and the filings do not say how much of the cash balance is customer advances.

fields.value: Deferred revenue, a non-interest-bearing float that funds operations, stood at USD 83.93 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 43.6 million at the end of 2025. Customers have prepaid against future deliveries, so part of the cash buffer is owed in product rather than available to creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity of USD 203.4 million at September 30, 2026 is cash of USD 158.2 million plus USD 45.2 million of availability under the asset-based facility, which has nothing drawn and matures in September 2028. Calls on it in the next quarter are the distribution of USD 18.9 million, fourth-quarter capital spending that the full-year estimate implies at USD 29.11 million to USD 38.11 million (the release outlook is USD 26 million to USD 34 million), and the semi-annual note coupon due in December. No principal on the notes or the facility falls due within twelve months: the notes mature in June 2028 and have been callable at par since June 15, 2026.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against caution is the balance sheet: net leverage of 1.83x is below the 2.67x of FY2024 and the 2.37x of FY2025, interest cover of 6.10x is above FY2024 and FY2025, and liquidity of USD 203.4 million is well above USD 117.1 million at the end of 2025. fields.value: The view would turn negative on a change of control, which the 2025 annual report says could follow a sale of the Icahn interest in CVR Energy: the 101% repurchase offer on the notes would call for about USD 555.5 million before accrued interest, against liquidity of USD 203.4 million, and the executed indenture that would settle the terms is not in the evidence. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance fact pack for Cvr Partners, Lp (CVR Partners, LP in its filings; issuer id uan-1425292), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, operating model, ownership, control, related-party arrangements, owner behaviour and history from the eight supplied filings and releases, with no specified transaction in the evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control rests with CVR Energy and Icahn Enterprises through the general partner, and the board's policy is to pay out all available cash, so creditor protection depends on debt covenants that are not in the evidence rather than on independent governance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is two nitrogen fertilizer plants selling mostly UAN and ammonia at commodity prices under contracts of less than one year, so cash flow follows prices and plant uptime. Distributions of USD 125.99 million in FY2025 exceeded free cash flow of USD 98.84 million, and the owners are weighing strategic options that could involve the Partnership; a sale of the Icahn interest in CVR Energy could trigger a repurchase offer on the notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 47–53; calculation A1; calculation A5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control is concentrated and creditors have no governance voice. CVR Energy holds about 37% of the units and all of the general partner, and Icahn Enterprises owns about 71% of CVR Energy and so is treated by the issuer as holding about 40% of the units beneficially. Unitholders do not elect the general partner or its directors, the partnership agreement replaces default fiduciary duties with narrower contractual ones, and the board rests on exemptions from the exchange's independence rules, so the only checks on owner decisions that creditors can rely on are the debt documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The board changed shape in October 2025, which tightens owner control. Four directors, three of them independent, were removed that month, the board is chaired by a current Icahn Enterprises employee, and at the end of 2025 the board of six held three independent directors, short of a majority, while a two-person special committee of the chair and the chief executive could approve urgent matters between board meetings at the date of the annual report. The documents give no reason for the removals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Related-party arrangements are a dependency as well as a cost. CVR Energy's refinery supplied about 36% of the pet coke used in 2025, the services agreement that provides management and administration can be ended on 90 days' notice, and the Coffeyville feedstock and hydrogen agreement ends automatically if the two parties fall out of common control. Charges to the Partnership were about USD 42.32 million in FY2025, 8.89% of cost of sales and administrative expense, and the CVR Energy subsidiary line rose from USD 8.9 million to USD 14.9 million in the first nine months of 2026, so a change of control would reach supply and services as well as the notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Distribution policy leaks cash in weak years but has not been debt funded. The board distributes available cash after reserves it sets in its sole discretion, and about 39% goes to CVR Energy and Icahn Enterprises. Distributions exceeded free cash flow in FY2023 and FY2025 and were met from cash, while borrowed debt stayed at the notes alone; in the first nine months of 2026 free cash flow of USD 193.88 million covered distributions of USD 110.45 million. The declared third-quarter distribution of USD 18.9 million follows a quarter in which USD 64.26 million was paid.

fields.value: Event risk comes from the owners' strategic review and the change-of-control terms, not from any disclosed transaction. CVR Energy and Icahn Enterprises say they are considering strategic transactions that may include options involving the Partnership, with no terms or timetable. A sale or transfer of some or all of the Icahn interest in CVR Energy could be a change of control under the notes, with a repurchase offer at 101%, and an event of default under the asset-based facility; the owners' general partner can also buy out public unitholders if it and its affiliates ever hold more than 80% of the units, which is far from the 40% held.

fields.value: Management is in transition. The chief executive named in the first-quarter release was succeeded by the chief financial officer by the second-quarter release, the second and third quarterly reports are signed by an interim chief financial officer, and executives are employed through CVR Energy, which sets the pay of every executive officer except the chief executive. The partnership bears these costs through service fees and the filings do not show a cost of the transition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model is a commodity price-taker with feedstock and plant concentration. Product sales are mostly UAN and ammonia under wholesale contracts of less than one year, the top two customers took 28% of FY2025 net sales, sales are heavier in the first half of each year, and each plant is a single site, so a turnaround or outage hits EBITDA in the quarter. Customers also prepay, which lifted deferred revenue to USD 83.93 million at September 30, 2026 from USD 43.6 million at the end of 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against concern is conduct: the documents read report no debt-funded distribution, no amendment or exchange of the notes, no drop-down of assets to an unrestricted subsidiary and no payment to the owners beyond their pro rata share of distributions and the charges under the service agreements, borrowed debt has been the one note issue since 2021, and the board sets reserves. The chain of ownership is also stable, with the shares of the holders unchanged to the level the filings print. That view would win if the owners' review ends without a transaction and the executed debt documents show tight restricted-payment and affiliate-transaction limits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment of Cvr Partners, Lp (CVR Partners, LP in its filings; issuer id uan-1425292), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business risk, cash-flow durability, liquidity, refinancing capacity, financial policy and the main downside path from the eight supplied filings and releases and the three earlier modules, without a rating, security view or legal-capacity conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit quality is adequate but volatile: moderate leverage, fixed-rate notes due in 2028 and liquidity of USD 203.4 million support creditors, while commodity-priced earnings and an owner-controlled payout leave little margin for a price or uptime shock.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was 1.83x last-twelve-months EBITDA at September 30, 2026 and interest cover was 6.10x, yet EBITDA fell 36.36% in FY2024 on a revenue fall of 22.91%, and distributions exceeded free cash flow in FY2023 and FY2025. The primary downside path is a price or outage shock that cuts EBITDA while distributions continue; a change of control would add a repurchase offer of about USD 555.5 million against liquidity of USD 203.4 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation B1; calculation B2; calculation B8; calculation B13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are the weakest dimension: revenue is exposed to commodity prices and plant uptime, and fixed plant costs turn a modest revenue move into a large EBITDA move. In FY2024 revenue fell 22.91% and EBITDA fell 36.36%, 1.59 times as fast, because direct operating expenses fell only 8.32%; EBITDA then recovered to USD 210.85 million in FY2025 and USD 224.73 million for the last twelve months. Customers contract for less than one year at fixed prices, the top two took 28% of FY2025 sales, and a turnaround or outage hits a single site.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 113; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B2; calculation B4; calculation B13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate and the debt is fixed rate, which is the strongest support. Total debt to EBITDA ranged from 1.95x in FY2023 to 3.18x in FY2024 and stood at 2.54x on the last-twelve-months basis, with net leverage of 1.83x; because the notes carry a fixed coupon, cover of EBITDA to cash interest moved only with EBITDA, from 5.24x at the low in FY2024 to 6.10x. Debt of USD 569.74 million includes finance lease obligations, and no principal falls due before June 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 104–106; calculation B1; calculation B13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is adequate and improving but rests on rising capital spending. Free cash flow was positive in every period, USD 219.33 million in FY2023, USD 98.84 million in FY2025 and USD 148.71 million for the last twelve months, equal to 78.03%, 46.87% and 66.17% of EBITDA. Cash capital expenditures rose from USD 50.8 million in FY2025 to USD 88.08 million over the last twelve months, and the 2026 estimate sits 66.89% to 82.7% above FY2025 spending, so conversion depends on the East Dubuque expansion and reliability projects paying back.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for the next two quarters and the refinancing window is distant but not remote. Liquidity of USD 203.4 million at September 30, 2026 is cash of USD 158.2 million plus availability under an undrawn asset-based facility; after the declared distribution of USD 18.9 million and fourth-quarter capital spending, cash would stand at USD 101.18 million to USD 110.18 million before any operating cash flow in the quarter. The notes mature 575 days after the as-of date and become a current liability in mid-2027, so refinancing capacity will be tested at the point the nitrogen cycle is least predictable.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 104; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation B7; calculation B13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the second weakness. Distributions of USD 281.36 million in FY2023 and USD 125.99 million in FY2025 exceeded free cash flow and were met from cash, about 39% went to CVR Energy and Icahn Enterprises, and the board can change the policy at any time. Customer prepayments lifted deferred revenue to USD 83.93 million at September 30, 2026, equal to 53.06% of the cash balance, so part of the cash buffer is owed in product and the working-capital inflow will reverse as deliveries are made.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation B10; calculation B11; calculation B13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Event risk is concentrated in control. The owners are considering strategic options that could involve the Partnership, with no terms stated, and a sale of the Icahn interest in CVR Energy could be a change of control under the notes with a repurchase offer of about USD 555.5 million; liquidity covers 36.61% of it. Supply and services from CVR Energy also depend on common control, so a change would reach operations as well as debt, and the executed debt documents that would settle the terms are not in the evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 115; calculation B8; calculation B13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is the balance sheet and the cost position. Net leverage of 1.83x is below its FY2024 and FY2025 levels, cover of 6.10x has recovered, free cash flow covered nine-month 2026 distributions, and U.S. natural gas prices keep a cost advantage for domestic producers while Middle East disruption has lifted fertilizer prices. That view would win if the East Dubuque expansion lifts output, prices stay firm through the fourth quarter and the owners' review ends without a transaction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; calculation B1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would turn negative if EBITDA fell again by the size seen in FY2024, which on last-twelve-months EBITDA would leave USD 143.03 million and take total debt to EBITDA to 3.98x and cover to 3.89x, or on any disclosed move in control. This is an illustration of the issuer's own history, not a forecast; the Downside module sets the stress properly.

fields.value: - No ratings, market prices or peer figures are supplied, so the assessments of business strength and of capital-market access are made against the issuer's own history only, which limits how confidently the profile can be called adequate rather than strong or weak.

fields.value: - Last-twelve-months figures come from unaudited stubs and include two turnaround-affected quarters, so last-twelve-months leverage is probably conservative against a year without turnarounds, while the unaudited stubs add reporting risk, which bears on the finding that leverage is moderate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The narrative steps and registers below carry the method's remaining outputs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CVR Partners makes and sells nitrogen fertilizer, mainly UAN and ammonia, from two plants: Coffeyville, Kansas, which gasifies pet coke, and East Dubuque, Illinois, which runs on natural gas. Revenue is wholesale, to retailers and distributors and to agricultural and industrial buyers, under contracts that generally fix price for less than one year, so revenue visibility is short and follows market prices within each season.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation follows the planting season, with higher sales in the first half, and is interrupted every few years by a planned turnaround at each plant. The business model therefore supports cash-flow visibility for a quarter or two, not for the length of the debt, and refinancing confidence depends on where the nitrogen price cycle stands when the notes become current.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Partnership is a listed limited partnership controlled by CVR Energy through the general partner, with Icahn Enterprises owning about 71% of CVR Energy. Public unitholders hold about 60% of the units but cannot elect the general partner or its directors, and the board was reshaped in October 2025. The financial-policy implication is that distributions, transactions and debt decisions are owner-led, and creditors are protected by the debt documents rather than by governance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: UAN is the largest product and is priced at the gate per ton, so revenue is a function of price, volume and mix, with no pass-through of feedstock cost. In the third quarter of 2026 lower UAN prices and ammonia volumes cut net sales by USD 17.4 million against the prior-year quarter, while for the nine months higher UAN and ammonia prices added USD 64.7 million; the revenue base is therefore cyclical and not contractually recurring, and the top two customers are 28% of sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins cannot be defended well under volume or price pressure because the plants carry high fixed operating costs: direct operating expenses excluding turnaround were 40.69% of FY2024 net sales against 34.21% in FY2023 after revenue fell. EBITDA margin was 41.25%, 34.06% and 34.79% in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025. Feedstock is a small part of cost, so margin depends mainly on price and utilization rather than input cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 113; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B3; calculation B4; calculation B13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Maintenance and growth capital spending are rising and turnaround costs are expensed in the quarter incurred, so conversion of EBITDA to free cash flow was 78.03% in FY2023 and 46.87% in FY2025. Management can defer growth projects and the board can cut distributions, which are the levers that protect liquidity; the issuer says it may adjust the timing or scope of growth capital projects.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 32; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B5; calculation B13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is high: domestic competitors, led by a much larger nitrogen producer, and subsidised imports compete on delivered price. Buyers are sophisticated and price focused, which caps pass-through; suppliers matter because CVR Energy's refinery supplies part of the pet coke; entry and substitution threats are limited for nitrogen itself. The credit consequence is a price-taker earnings profile with no pricing power to defend cash flow in a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulatory and geopolitical factors do alter credit risk here: Middle East supply disruption and import tariffs have supported U.S. prices, and litigation over an October 2025 ammonia release and a Kansas environmental class action carry unquantified liability. These items change liquidity and earnings risk and so are treated as material.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are fixed-rate debt with no maturity before June 2028, moderate leverage, positive free cash flow in every period, an undrawn facility and domestic feedstock. Weaknesses are volatile EBITDA, high fixed costs, owner-controlled payouts and a short contract tenor. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the East Dubuque expansion and firm prices; threats are a price or outage shock, a change of control and the unquantified lawsuits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Assessed on the nine dimensions: scale and market position Average; competitive advantage Average; business diversification Weak, with two plants, one segment and two products; cost and capex flexibility Average, because growth projects can be deferred while direct costs are largely fixed; margin stability Weak; free cash flow stability Average; ability to refinance Average, untested and dependent on the price cycle; liquidity position Average; financial policy and governance Weak. The main supports are leverage and liquidity, the main constraints are earnings volatility and owner control, the trend in leverage is improving from FY2024, and the missing datapoints are the debt documents, ratings and peer figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In the next twelve to twenty-four months the tailwinds are firm prices from supply disruption, the expansion adding about 5% of ammonia capacity and the end of the turnaround; the headwinds are a normalisation of prices, higher capital spending and the lawsuits. Over three to five years the notes mature in 2028, the Coffeyville dual-feedstock project is planned for construction in 2028 and the owners' strategic review is unresolved. Management expects fourth-quarter ammonia utilization of 88% to 93% and says nitrogen supplies remain tight, which is management language and not evidence of price direction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario is a nitrogen price fall or a plant outage of the kind that cut FY2024 EBITDA. The first operational break is lower realized gate prices or lost tons at a single site; because direct operating costs are largely fixed, EBITDA falls faster than revenue; free cash flow then drops below the distribution the board has declared, and cash covers the gap, as it did in FY2023 and FY2025. Leverage rises and cover falls as shown in the illustration, the facility's availability of USD 45.2 million is the next buffer, and the notes become current in mid-2027 while earnings are weak. The board can cut distributions and defer growth projects, which should avoid liquidity distress at current cash, but a change of control in the same window would add the repurchase offer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B2; calculation B9; calculation B11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, CVR Partners presents an adequate business profile supported by fixed-rate debt with no maturity before 2028, moderate leverage and positive free cash flow, but credit quality is constrained by commodity-priced and operationally concentrated earnings, an owner-controlled payout and unseen debt terms. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in the near term and weak through a full cycle. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the nitrogen price level and the owners' plans in 2027. The primary downside path is a price or outage shock with distributions continuing and a change of control in the same window. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, ratings and market prices.

fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment completed with limitations. Top risk: an earnings shock while distributions continue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths, ranked. First, fixed-rate notes of USD 550.0 million with no maturity before June 2028 and an undrawn facility: interest cost is fixed, so cover of 6.10x moves only with EBITDA, and no refinancing is needed for 575 days. Second, moderate leverage of 1.83x net on last-twelve-months EBITDA, which leaves room to absorb a moderate decline. Third, positive free cash flow in every period, USD 148.71 million over the last twelve months, which funds capital spending and most distributions. Fourth, liquidity of USD 203.4 million, which comfortably exceeds the known calls of the fourth quarter.

fields.value: Weaknesses, ranked. First, volatile EBITDA on high fixed costs: EBITDA fell 36.36% in FY2024 on a revenue fall of 22.91%, which is the path to a liquidity or refinancing problem. Second, owner control with a variable distribution policy that exceeded free cash flow in two of three fiscal years, so creditors rely on cash rather than retained earnings. Third, change-of-control exposure of about USD 555.5 million with owners reviewing options. Fourth, rising capital spending and a working-capital inflow from prepayments that will reverse. Fifth, unseen debt documents and no ratings or market prices.
